title: "Parsing VEP Output to Classify cis vs. trans"
output: html_notebook

Parsing VEP Output to Classify cis vs. trans in R
Key Rule:
    A cis variant is within ±500kb of the affected gene (may use 1Mb).
    A trans variant is outside this window.

Sample R script
```{r}
library(data.table)
library(GenomicRanges)

# Load VEP output
vep <- fread("annotated.vep.txt", fill = TRUE)

# Example columns: 'Location', 'SYMBOL', 'Feature_type', 'Consequence'
# Extract chromosome and position
vep[, c("chr", "pos") := tstrsplit(Location, ":", fixed = TRUE)]
vep[, pos := as.integer(pos)]

# Load GTF with gene coordinates (or use biomaRt)
gtf <- fread("genes.gtf")  # Should contain gene name, chr, start, end
setnames(gtf, c("gene", "chr", "start", "end"))

# Merge and classify
vep_annot <- merge(vep, gtf, by.x = "SYMBOL", by.y = "gene", all.x = TRUE)

# Calculate distance to gene
vep_annot[, distance := abs(pos - ((start + end) / 2))]

# Classify
vep_annot[, cis_trans := ifelse(distance <= 500000, "cis", "trans")]
table(vep_annot$cis_trans)

```



Script to Annotate VEP Output with GTEx eQTLs
GTEx Resources:
    Download GTEx eQTL files from https://www.gtexportal.org/home/downloads/adult-gtex/qtl (e.g., GTEx_Analysis_v8_eQTL.tar or  GTEx_Analysis_v8_eQTL.tar or  *.signif_variant_gene_pairs.txt.gz)
  
  
```{bash}
# Download all GTEx v8 cis-eQTLs (around 1.6 GB compressed)
wget https://storage.googleapis.com/gtex_analysis_v8/single_tissue_qtl_data/GTEx_Analysis_v8_eQTL.tar

# Unpack the archive
tar -xvf GTEx_Analysis_v8_eQTL.tar

```


Python Script: annotate_with_gtex.py

```{python}

import pandas as pd

# Load VEP output (from --tab flag)
vep = pd.read_csv("annotated.vep.txt", sep="\t", comment="#")

# Parse VEP column 'Location' into CHR and POS
vep[['CHR', 'POS']] = vep['Location'].str.split(":", expand=True)
vep['POS'] = vep['POS'].astype(int)

# Load GTEx eQTLs
gtex = pd.read_csv("GTEx_Analysis_v10_eQTL/signif_variant_gene_pairs.txt.gz", sep="\t")
gtex[['CHR', 'POS', 'REF', 'ALT']] = gtex['variant_id'].str.split('_', expand=True)
gtex['POS'] = gtex['POS'].astype(int)

# Join by CHR and POS
merged = pd.merge(vep, gtex, on=["CHR", "POS"], how="left")

# Save merged output
merged.to_csv("vep_annotated_with_gtex.csv", index=False)

```
